items.prompt: A Warband process is started with ROLE=resolver. Does it run the database migrations when it boots?
items.answer: Yes; initialize() runs before the role is even read
distractors: No; only the api role calls initialize() during boot
Only when ROLE is all, which is the default role
No; migrations run from a separate CLI step only
items.explanation: index.ts calls await initialize() on line 16, and reads process.env.ROLE on the next line, so every role migrates at boot.

items.prompt: Does a process started with ROLE=resolver answer HTTP requests to /api/health and /metrics?
items.answer: Yes, both: every role builds the app and listens on its PORT
distractors: Only /metrics, because health checks are limited to api roles
Neither, since a resolver process never calls app.listen()
Only /api/health, because metrics install only for api roles
items.explanation: buildApp(), installMetrics(app) and app.listen() run unconditionally in index.ts, so a resolver serves the whole /api surface and /metrics.

items.prompt: The browser receives a WebSocket message that is not a server_time or connected heartbeat. What does the client do with the message contents?
items.answer: Ignores the payload and asks React Query to refetch server state
distractors: Merges the outbox payload directly into the cached query data
Applies the payload only when it is newer than the cached state
Keeps it in the Zustand store until the next poll confirms it
items.explanation: socket.onmessage only calls refreshRef.current?.request(), which invalidates and refetches queries. The message is a hint; PostgreSQL state read through /api/state is the truth.

items.prompt: On main, tab A opens the WebSocket, then tab B opens it for the same player, then tab A closes. What does sockets.get(player) hold afterwards?
items.answer: One Set that now holds only B; the map entry stays
distractors: No entry: the close handler of A deletes the player key
A Set still holding A and B until the heartbeat fires
A new Set holding B that replaced the Set A was using
items.explanation: The second connection finds the existing Set and adds to it, so both handlers share one Set. A deletes itself; the Set still has B, so !set.size is false and the entry is kept.

items.prompt: warband_event_lag_seconds has buckets [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60]. 1,000 events each resolve exactly 0.3 s late. What does histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) return?
items.answer: About 0.4975 s, interpolated inside the 0.25 to 0.5 bucket
distractors: Exactly 0.3 s, the true lag that every event observed
0.5 s, the upper bound of the bucket that holds them all
0.25 s, the lower bound of the bucket that holds them all
items.explanation: Every observation lands in (0.25, 0.5]. Linear interpolation at rank 0.99 gives 0.25 + 0.25 x 0.99 = 0.4975; the histogram cannot know the real value was 0.3.

items.prompt: With the same buckets (top finite bucket 60), 1,000 events each resolve 90 s late. What does histogram_quantile(0.99, ...) return, and what follows for an alert written as > 120?
items.answer: It returns 60, so an alert on > 120 can never fire
distractors: It returns 90, so the alert fires once lag passes 120
It returns +Inf, so the alert fires on every evaluation
It returns NaN, so the alert reports no data instead
items.explanation: When the target rank falls in the +Inf bucket, histogram_quantile returns the upper bound of the highest finite bucket, 60. An alert threshold above the top bucket is unreachable.

items.prompt: warband_lock_retries_total reads 0 during heavy resolver lock contention. According to the code, why?
items.answer: resolveDue calls transaction(fn, 1), so the retry branch never runs
distractors: The gauge is reset on every scrape, so it reads 0 between the retries
Retries are counted for deadlocks (40P01) but not lock timeouts
The counter is incremented inside a transaction that rolls back
items.explanation: dbCounters.retries++ runs only when attempt < maxAttempts - 1. With maxAttempts = 1 that is never true, and resolveDue catches 40001/55P03/WB_BUSY and returns 0 with no metric.

items.prompt: Yesterday's release applied 013_npc_players.sql. Today someone adds a single comment line to the top of that file. What happens when any role starts?
items.answer: initialize() throws Applied migration was modified, and boot fails
distractors: It re-runs 013 as-is, since a comment does not change the SQL
It logs a warning, skips 013, and goes on to apply later files
It records the new checksum for 013 and continues with 014
items.explanation: The checksum is sha256 over the raw file text, so a comment changes it. prior.checksum !== checksum throws, and the top-level await in index.ts rejects.

items.prompt: Boot throws at migration 013. Can migrations that ran earlier in that same boot be left committed?
items.answer: No, because initialize() runs every migration in one transaction
distractors: Yes, because each migration file commits in its own separate transaction
Yes, though only the schema_migrations table creation survives
No, because migrations run in reverse order, so file 013 is run first
items.explanation: initialize() is a single transaction(async (tx) => ...) call, so the throw rolls back everything it did, including the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. The files are sorted ascending.

items.prompt: Which check does the /api/health handler in game.ts actually perform before answering ok?
items.answer: A single SELECT 1 query against the Postgres database
distractors: A check that the resolver loop ran in the last minute
A count of unsent outbox rows against a fixed threshold
A Redis PING, so Caddy can drain instances on Redis loss
items.explanation: get_api_health runs await database.query("SELECT 1") and returns { ok: true, server_now }. It checks nothing else.

items.prompt: Redis is down. Does per-player command rate limiting still work, and is the count shared by both api instances?
items.answer: Yes; takeLimit falls back to a shared Postgres rate_buckets row
distractors: No; limits are skipped so the engine keeps serving every player
Partly; each instance counts hits in its own in-memory map
No; each rate-limited request fails with 503 until Redis is back
items.explanation: When redis.isReady is false (or eval throws), takeLimit upserts into rate_buckets in Postgres, which both instances share. The comment says Redis loss must not remove abuse controls.

items.prompt: What happens to unsent outbox rows while Redis is unreachable?
items.answer: They stay unsent in Postgres and get published once Redis is back
distractors: The relay marks them sent, so the backlog cannot grow without limit
They move to a BullMQ retry queue that is held in process memory
They are deleted, since clients poll /api/state every 10 s anyway
items.explanation: The relay interval returns early when !redis.isReady, so nothing selects or updates the rows; sent_at stays NULL until a later tick publishes them.

items.prompt: The resolver query filters world_id=1 AND status='pending' AND due_at<=now, ordered by due_at,id with a LIMIT. Why does the partial index events_due ON scheduled_events(world_id,due_at,id) WHERE status='pending' fit it well?
items.answer: It is already in query order and leaves out every done row
distractors: It lets Postgres skip the LIMIT, since it stores row counts
It enforces one pending event per village at the database
It covers payload, so the query never reads the table heap
items.explanation: Equality on world_id then (due_at,id) order lets Postgres walk the index and stop after LIMIT rows with no sort, and the WHERE predicate keeps the growing history of done rows out of the index.

items.front: List the hops from a committed outbox row to the defender's browser re-reading /api/state.
items.back: Relay loop: SELECT unsent outbox rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, redis.publish to warband:events, UPDATE sent_at. Each api/ws subscriber: parse, send to every open socket in sockets.get(player_id). Browser onmessage: refreshRef.request(). queryRefresh: invalidate and refetch active queries, GET /api/state.

items.front: Which two timers can close a Warband WebSocket on main, and with what close code?
items.back: heartbeat: every 5 s re-runs authenticate(req); on failure close(4001, "Session revoked or expired"). expiry: a timeout at the JWT exp; close(4001, "Session refresh required").

items.front: What does docs/architecture.md say PostgreSQL owns and what Redis is allowed to hold?
items.back: PostgreSQL owns village aggregates, scheduled events, reports, idempotency records and the notification outbox. Redis holds only disposable caches, queue delivery state and invalidation hints; flushing Redis does not change the world.

items.front: What does committedResolutions(events) record for each event, and what does Math.max(0, ...) protect?
items.back: One lag sample per event: (now - due) / 1000 seconds, with the kind, observed into eventLag and passed to the registered observer. Math.max(0, ...) clamps an event due in the future (clock skew) to 0 instead of a negative lag.
